claim_statement: Amplifying the alpha-helix feature set (sigma_proj-unit dosing) during autoregressive DNA generation increases the encoded protein's pLDDT-weighted alpha-helix fraction, monotonically up to a mapped interior optimum, reproduced across two structure predictors.
variant_metric: ESMFold Spearman rho=0.867 p=0.0012 delta+0.144 at c*; OmegaFold rho=0.903 p=0.0003 delta+0.147 at c*; both significant, both positive, dual-predictor agree
delta: ESMFold: rho unchanged (0.867), delta slightly higher (+0.144 vs +0.129); OmegaFold: rho higher (0.903 vs 0.879), delta slightly higher (+0.147 vs +0.135) — consistent direction, same significance level
reasoning: Under the H-only helix definition (strict alpha only), the Spearman dose-response trend is ESMFold rho=0.867 (p=0.0012) and OmegaFold rho=0.903 (p=0.0003), both significant and in the same positive direction as the main experiment. The delta at c*=21.48 is slightly larger (+0.144/+0.147) under H-only vs HGI (+0.129/+0.135), which is expected because G/I helices contribute a noisy background that is removed under H-only, sharpening the signal. The main experiment's conclusion (positive monotone dose-response to interior c*, dual-predictor agreement) is reproduced under H-only. C2 is supported.
